meta.title: Bulgarian Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 143 expressions · 51 everyday, 60 verbs with се, 19 idioms, 13 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 143 Bulgarian set phrases, reflexive verbs, idioms and proverbs, in four subdecks: 51 everyday phrases, 60 verbs with се, 19 idioms and 13 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Bulgarian → English (see the Bulgarian, recall the meaning) and English → Bulgarian (see an English meaning, recall the Bulgarian) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the five level decks, Bulgarian A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is a list of single words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the five, so the two can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the everyday formulas, greetings and wishes and the multi-word adverbs and conjunctions a sentence is joined with (за да, как си, камо ли …). The VERBS WITH СЕ are reflexive verbs Wiktionary enters under their own headword, whose meaning is often not the plain verb's (надявам се, страхувам се, боя се …), given like every Bulgarian verb in the first person singular. The IDIOMS are expressions whose meaning is not their words' (Весела Коледа, имам се с някого, и така нататък …), and the PROVERBS the sayings Wiktionary files as proverbs (кръвта вода не става, приятел в нужда се познава, здрав дух в здраво тяло …). The deck is small because Wiktionary's Bulgarian holds few expressions, and it does not pad them out with composed ones. Within each subdeck the expressions come in the order of how many of Tatoeba's Bulgarian sentences contain them, a verb being counted in any of its forms; only 45 of the 143 are found there at all, and the rest follow in the order of how common their words are in film and television subtitles. Every expression is printed in Cyrillic with its stress marked. Real example sentences come with 43 of the 143 expressions, three apiece for 17, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Expressions, meanings, stress and the idiom and proverb labels: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Order: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, then a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba, CC BY 2.0 FR.
